connection_condition: question rows are the posts rows whose PostTypeId equals 1
description: A question is a specific kind of post; its value domain is a subset of the post domain (42912 of 91966 rows).

connection_condition: answer rows are the posts rows whose PostTypeId equals 2
description: An answer is a specific kind of post; its value domain is a subset of the post domain (47755 of 91966 rows).

connection_condition: every AcceptedAnswerId references a post whose PostTypeId equals 2
description: An accepted answer is a specific kind of answer: the whole accepted-answer domain is drawn from answer posts, never from questions or auxiliary post types.

connection_condition: bounty events are the votes rows whose VoteTypeId is 8 or 9
description: A bounty event is a specific kind of vote row; bounty amounts appear only on the start and close vote types, never on other vote types.

connection_condition: an answer's ParentId equals the Id of the question it replies to
description: A question is a whole composed of its answers; an answer cannot exist without the question it belongs to. 47749 of 47755 answers resolve to an existing question parent.

connection_condition: a comment's PostId equals the Id of the post it belongs to
description: A post is a whole composed of its comments; a comment has no meaning without its post. Comments attach mainly to questions and answers and only rarely to other post types.

connection_condition: a revision's PostId equals the Id of the post it records a change to
description: A post is a whole composed of its recorded revisions; a revision row has no meaning detached from its post.

connection_condition: a vote's PostId equals the Id of the post it was cast on
description: A post is a whole composed of the votes cast on it; every vote row resolves to an existing post, though only a minority of posts appear in the votes table at all.

connection_condition: a badge award's UserId equals the Id of the user receiving it
description: A user's record is composed of their badge awards; an award row is meaningless without the user it was granted to, and every UserId in badges resolves to a users row.

connection_condition: a question carries a tag when the tag name appears in its Tags text as a token wrapped in angle brackets; there is no junction table between tags and posts
description: Tags label questions through the denormalized Tags text rather than through a foreign key, so the connection is real but structurally indirect.
The usage count of a tag is derived from the number of questions that carry that tag; the stored value approximates a recount over the Tags text with small discrepancies.
A question's answer count is derived as the number of answers whose ParentId is that question; the stored value agreed exactly with this derivation for every question.

A post's score is conceptually derived from the votes cast on it (up-votes minus down-votes), but the votes table in this database is a partial snapshot, so the stored score cannot be reproduced from it in most cases.

connection_condition: a link's PostId is the source post and RelatedPostId is the related post; both are intended to reference posts rows
description: A post link connects two posts; the endpoints are overwhelmingly questions, with only five rows linking to an answer, and four rows point at posts that do not exist.

connection_condition: an acceptance is additionally recorded as a vote row whose VoteTypeId equals 1 and whose PostId is the accepted answer
description: Acceptance is represented twice, but with very different coverage: the question-side AcceptedAnswerId covers 14697 questions whereas the vote-side representation covers only 1451 accepted answers, because the votes table spans a narrow time window.
A user owns posts as their author, but the connection is optional: 1392 posts have no owner, and the sentinel account with Id -1 owns 211 posts.
